2027 Kawasaki KLE500 Lands with a Smarter Way to (Not) Use the Clutch
13 photos
Photo: Kawasaki
It’s been exactly a year since Japanese bike maker Kawasaki brought back the KLE500 dual-purpose motorcycle, and things are going so well that the company has now announced a new version is joining the range for the 2027 model year.
Until now, the revived KLE500 was a pretty small family, with only two models on the table: the standard and SE. Now, the SE Smartride variant is joining the party, bringing along a smarter way of (not) using the clutch.
Kawasaki calls it the Smartride, basically a self-engaging clutch system that works using a mechanical centrifugal clutch fitted inside a conventional assembly. Doing things this way is first and foremost supposed to reduce the need to use the clutch in high-intensity moments such as stop-and-go urban riding.
Then, it removes the need for delicate half-clutch control when pulling away from a stop, effectively taking clutch lever operation out of the equation. Naturally, normal shifting of gears with the use of the clutch is still on the table when riding.
Other than the fitting of the Smartride tech on this model for the first time, the KLE500 is still new enough to continue unchanged mechanically. That means we’re still dealing with a high-tensile steel trellis frame holding a fuel-injected 451cc parallel-twin engine.
The motorcycle rides on spoked wheels sized 21 inches at the front and 17 inches at the rear, which are supported by a KYB 43 mm inverted front fork with 210 mm of travel and a Uni-Trak rear system with 200 mm of travel. Stopping power is supplied by disc brakes with selectable ABS . For the new model year, Kawasaki is adding tubeless tires to the mix.
The bike’s design continues to be inspired by the worlds of rallying and motocross, and that means it also includes a skid plate and a tall front cowl for protection. There is also a windscreen on deck with three adjustable levels, and a fuel tank capable of holding 4.2 gallons (almost 16 liters).
The addition of the Smartride tech is, for now at least, limited to the European market. Over in the U.S., the two-wheeler continues to soldier on in its 2026 model year incarnation, with pricing set at $6,599 for the standard two-wheeler and $7,499 for the SE.
This one, short for Special Edition, adds a taller windshield, metal-reinforced hand guards, a larger skid plate, and LED lights. The LCD instrumentation on the standard is replaced by a 4.3-inch TFT screen. The color choices remain the same as before.
The Europeans are also treated to Edition machines in three distinct versions: Rally (Akrapovic titanium exhaust, radiator cover, and low passenger seat), Adventure Tourer (engine guard and a pair of two-liter panniers), and Top Case, carrying, as the name says, a top case.
